title: Codex subscription auth for agent spawns
description: V0.2 REQUIREMENT RECORD (human, REPL 2026-08-19): the fleet must be able to run Codex agents on an OpenAI/Codex SUBSCRIPTION seat, not only API keys — same requirement as the Claude subscription support landing in v0.1 (epic-fbe4fc13 task-1502d1ea). PARKED BY THE SCOPE FREEZE: the Codex adapter itself is M4/v0.2 portability scope. When v0.2 opens, plan against fresh measurement: how the Codex CLI authenticates a subscription seat headlessly (login/token flow at that time), what env vars its spawner honors, and whether the wrapper's spawn allowlist (agent-spawn-environment.ts prefix list) forwards them. The Claude-side pattern to mirror: subscription token minted interactively once, carried by env, launcher accepts any-of the credential set, provenance names the variable never the value. Do not build against this record without re-measuring — the CLI auth landscape moves.
taskRails: BACKLOG until the v0.2 scope opens; governor approval required to promote per the freeze rails.
Re-measure the Codex CLI auth flow at promotion time; this record's mechanics are stale by default.

implementationPlan.note:
CODEX CLI AUTH RE-MEASUREMENT (2026-08-20, real binary C:\Users\Yaron\AppData\Local\Programs\OpenAI\Codex\bin\codex.exe). No credential VALUE printed anywhere below.

(1) VERSION — `codex --version` -> `codex-cli 0.147.0` EXIT=0.

(2) HEADLESS/SUBSCRIPTION PATH — `codex login --help`:
```
Commands:  status  Show login status
Options:
      --with-api-key      Read the API key from stdin (e.g. `printenv OPENAI_API_KEY | codex login --with-api-key`)
      --with-access-token Read the access token from stdin (e.g. `printenv CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN | codex login --with-access-token`)
      --device-auth
```
So THREE mint paths exist: interactive browser login, `--device-auth` (device code), and stdin token/key. Top-level `codex --help` also lists `logout`, `doctor`, `exec` (non-interactive run).

(3) WHERE CREDENTIALS PERSIST — `CODEX_HOME` is the carrier, PROVEN load-bearing, not assumed:
 - default home `C:\Users\Yaron\.codex\` contains `auth.json` (4083 bytes, listing only; contents never read).
 - `codex login status` (default home, non-interactive shell) -> `Logged in using ChatGPT` EXIT=0. This IS the headless read of a SUBSCRIPTION seat.
 - `CODEX_HOME=<empty temp dir> codex login status` -> `Not logged in` EXIT=1, and the probe dir stayed EMPTY (no files created). Redirecting CODEX_HOME fully redirects auth resolution.
 - `codex exec --help` states it verbatim: "Do not load `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml`; auth still uses `CODEX_HOME`". The CLI's own help binds auth resolution to CODEX_HOME.

(4) ENV VARS HONORED FOR AUTH — measured two ways.
 a. Live probes with empty CODEX_HOME + obviously-fake sentinels:
    `OPENAI_API_KEY=<sentinel>` -> `Not logged in` EXIT=1 (not consulted by `login status`)
    `CODEX_API_KEY=<sentinel>`  -> `Not logged in` EXIT=1
    `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN=<sentinel>` -> `Error checking login status: invalid agent identity JWT format` EXIT=1  <-- READ AND PARSED. Env-honored, expects a JWT.
 b. Binary string table (`grep -a -o -E '\b(OPENAI|CODEX|CHATGPT)_[A-Z0-9_]{2,40}\b'`, unique+counted):
    CODEX_HOME 61 | OPENAI_API_KEY 19 | CODEX_MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION 14 | CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN 4 | CODEX_SQLITE_HOME 3 | CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE 3 | CODEX_URL 2 | CODEX_INTERNAL_ORIGINATOR_OVERRIDE 2 | CODEX_AUTH 1 | CODEX_API_KEY 1 | CODEX_CA_CERTIFICATE 1 | CODEX_GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN 1 | ... and the decisive one:
    `OPENAI_API_KEYCODEX_API_KEYCODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN` 1 — a Rust string-pool concatenation showing the three auth env names ADJACENT. The CLI's auth env set is exactly {OPENAI_API_KEY, CODEX_API_KEY, CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN}.
    ZERO `CHATGPT_*` env names exist in the binary -> step 4 must NOT add a "CHATGPT_" prefix. `chatgpt_account_id` (14) is a config/auth.json FIELD, not an env var.

(5) DOES A SUBSCRIPTION SEAT RUN HEADLESSLY? YES. `codex login status` returned `Logged in using ChatGPT` EXIT=0 from a non-interactive shell against on-disk state minted by an earlier interactive login. Exactly the Claude-side analogue ("minted interactively once, carried by env") with ONE structural difference that drives the design: Claude carries a TOKEN VALUE in a variable; Codex carries a STATE DIRECTORY PATH in `CODEX_HOME`. NOT blocked — a headless path exists.

CONSEQUENCE FOR STEPS 3-4: the two prefixes to forward are `OPENAI_` and `CODEX_` (both required — `CODEX_` alone drops OPENAI_API_KEY, `OPENAI_` alone drops CODEX_HOME/CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN). The Codex any-of gate set, subscription first per the Claude precedent: CODEX_HOME, CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, CODEX_API_KEY.

implementationPlan.note:
LANDED CLAUDE PATTERN MEASURED (all line numbers at HEAD 5d35739).

A. THE ANY-OF SET SHAPE — moe-up-env.ts:72-79
```
const CLAUDE_CREDENTIAL_VARIABLES = Object.freeze([
  "CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN", "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN", "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY",
] as const);
const ALIAS_CREDENTIAL = "CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN";
const DELIVERED_CREDENTIAL = "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN";
const CREDENTIAL_HINT = "(set one; run `claude setup-token` for a subscription token)";
```
CLOSED roster, subscription first / api key last. `present()` (:85-88) treats EMPTY as absent. `claudeCredentials()` (:142-160) walks the roster in order, takes the FIRST present as a `secretEntry(name,"PRESET",value)`, returns null when none present. Alias mapping is Claude-specific (the CLI ignores the alias under --bare) — Codex needs no such mapping, its names are honored directly.

B. THE GATE — moe-up-env.ts:103-107 + :175-178
```
function isClaudeCommand(command)  // basename, strip extension, lowercase === "claude"
const credentials = isClaudeCommand(agentCommand.value) ? claudeCredentials(env) : [];
if (credentials === null) return { ok:false, refusals:[refuseCredential()] };
```
CRITICAL: the `: []` arm means a NON-claude MOE_AGENT_COMMAND waives the credential entirely — so `MOE_AGENT_COMMAND=codex` is UNGATED today. That `: []` is exactly where the Codex arm hooks in. Accepted entries flow into `variables` (:180-189) and then verbatim into the child `overlay` (:191-192), so a gate entry IS the delivery mechanism.

C. PROVENANCE — moe-up-env.ts:222-229 `describeLaunchVariables`
`entry.secret ? "<${SOURCE_WORD[source]}, hidden>" : entry.value` — a secret entry prints `NAME=<preset, hidden>`; the value never reaches the console. Refusal (:109-119) carries stable code `MOE_UP_ENV_MISSING`, `variable` = the roster joined by ", ", message = `CODE: names hint`. Names only, never values.

D. MOE-UP-MAIN NEEDS NO CHANGE — moe-up-main.ts:160-173: `runMoeUp` calls `resolveLaunchEnv`, and on `!ok` loops `for (const refusal of resolution.refusals) options.log(refusal.message)` then returns 1. Provider-agnostic already. Confirms plan step-4 item (3) is a no-op: mirror inside moe-up-env.ts, do not restructure.

E. TESTS THAT PIN THE BEHAVIOR
 - moe-up-env.test.ts (270 lines): `resolved()`/`refused()` helpers; ACCEPTED_VARIABLES + REFUSAL_MESSAGE hand-written (:42-45) deliberately NOT rebuilt from the roster; acceptance table :194-209 asserts source PRESET + secret true + `NAME=<preset, hidden>`; :250-269 is the no-value sweep WITH a vacuity floor `expect(lines.length).toBeGreaterThan(8)`. :154 "needs no credential at all once MOE_AGENT_COMMAND names a non-claude command" uses `"node"` — stays green under a codex-only new gate.
 - THE ALLOWLIST IS PINNED IN agent-spawner.test.ts:150-207, NOT in a dedicated file. There is NO `agent-spawn-environment.test.ts`; the pin is a strict `expect(child.options.env).toEqual({ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB, NO_PROXY, no_proxy})` reached through `claudeSpawner`, with `GITHUB_TOKEN: "unrelated-secret-must-not-reach-agent"` as the existing negative control. `agentEnvironment` has exactly one production consumer: agent-spawner.ts:115.
 - No line-count sweep guard exists under apps/daemon (the readdirSync/250 hits in agent-spawner.test.ts are config-dir emptiness assertions). The `packages/core/src/planning` size guard is planning-only, so a new test file here is unconstrained by it. `agent-spawn-environment.js` bridge ALREADY exists (46 bytes) so the module is already runtime-tier — no new bridge is demanded.

F. OVERLAP CHECK (reopenReason) — SETTLED, ZERO overlap.
`grep -rn -E 'OPENAI|CODEX' apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/` returns exactly ONE line: `verifier-process-runner.test.ts:66: OPENAI_API_KEY: "other-provider-secret"`. That is a DIFFERENT and stricter allowlist (createVerifierProcessRunner, no agentEnvironment call — verified: agentEnvironment has only the one consumer above) and its assertion is `toMatchObject` on `{LANG, Path, TMPDIR}`, so this task's prefix edit cannot touch it. 1502d1ea landed nothing Codex-side.

implementationPlan.note:
RED CONFIRMED. `pnpm exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/orchestrator/moe-up-env.test.ts src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-environment.test.ts` (cwd apps/daemon) -> EXIT=1, count line verbatim: `Test Files  2 failed (2)` / `Tests  18 failed | 25 passed (43)`.

MEASUREMENT OVERRODE THE PLAN'S EXAMPLES on two points, per the step's own rule:
 1. The plan wrote "e.g. CODEX_HOME/auth-file presence or seat token variable". The measurement settled it: the SUBSCRIPTION arm is `CODEX_HOME` (a PATH to the state dir holding auth.json), not a token variable. So the any-of set mixes one path and three secrets, unlike Claude's three-token set.
 2. The plan allowed a "CHATGPT_" prefix "only if step 1 measured the CLI honoring one". Zero CHATGPT_* env names exist in the binary -> NOT added. The measured set is exactly two prefixes: OPENAI_ and CODEX_.
Shipped any-of set, subscription first / api key last: `CODEX_HOME, CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, CODEX_API_KEY`.

PROVENANCE DESIGN NOTE: all four codex entries are asserted `secret: true`, INCLUDING CODEX_HOME. A path is not a credential, but it names the directory holding the seat, and one uniform rule makes the sentinel-absence sweep total instead of leaving one unmasked hole in it.

(a) FORWARDING - new file `agent-spawn-environment.test.ts` (7 RED cases), unit-level on `agentEnvironment`:
 - four `forwards <NAME> to the spawned agent process` cases, one per measured variable;
 - `forwards the whole codex set at once and nothing else it was not given` pins the EXACT key set (toSorted().toEqual) so a future pass-through addition must be declared before it goes green;
 - NEGATIVE CONTROLS so the sweep cannot prove only additions: `still strips an unlisted variable while forwarding the codex set beside it` (GITHUB_TOKEN + OPERATOR_CREDENTIAL) and `still strips MOE_ authority in either case alongside the codex set` (MOE_DAEMON_CREDENTIAL, MOE_STORE_PATH, lowercase moe_daemon_credential);
 - `keeps forwarding the provider prefixes it already carried before codex` (ANTHROPIC_/AWS_/AZURE_/GOOGLE_/VERTEX_) is a deliberate already-GREEN regression guard against a prefix-list rewrite dropping the incumbents.

(b) THE GATE - moe-up-env.test.ts `resolveLaunchEnv codex credential acceptance` (9 RED cases): four accept-alone cases asserting source PRESET + secret true + `NAME=<preset, hidden>` + the value reaching `config.env[name]` (the overlay IS the delivery path); the refusal arm asserting code === MOE_UP_ENV_MISSING, variable === "CODEX_HOME, CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, CODEX_API_KEY" and the full hand-written message; empty-is-absent; codex named by absolute path / .cmd / .EXE; presence order (all four set -> CODEX_HOME reported, other three toBeUndefined).

(c) PROVENANCE - `prints no codex credential value on any disclosure or refusal line` feeds all four sentinels, sweeps disclosure lines + the refusal message, and carries the vacuity floor `expect(lines.length).toBeGreaterThan(8)` before looking for values, mirroring the claude sweep.

(d) COEXISTENCE - new describe `resolveLaunchEnv keeps the two provider gates apart` (4 cases): codex command + ONLY claude credentials -> refuses naming the CODEX set; claude command + ONLY codex credentials -> refuses naming the CLAUDE set; `hands a codex seat no claude variable and a claude token no codex variable` pins both overlays as exact key sets; `leaves a command that is neither claude nor codex ungated` keeps the `node` waiver.

RED reasons verified as missing-feature, not typos: the gate cases die on `Error: expected a refusal, got a launch config` (a codex command is UNGATED today - the `: []` arm at moe-up-env.ts:175), and the forwarding cases die on `expected undefined to be '<value>'` / key-set diffs missing the CODEX_/OPENAI_ names (the prefix list at agent-spawn-environment.ts:21-23 strips them). Two new cases were GREEN on arrival by design and are labelled above as regression guards, not RED claims.
